text:
maria: Hey team, quick question - my corporate card shows a charge for an Airbnb I booked for a vendor visit: $420 on 2026-03-05. The host issued a partial refund of $120 on 2026-03-06 but the card portal still shows the full $420 and no pending credit. I submitted the expense for $300 (net) but the payment team flagged it. Any guidance?

ben_finance: thanks for calling it out, @maria. we need the refund proof and the host transaction id. can you paste the Airbnb refund email or screenshot? also include the card txn id and the refund txn id if available.

maria: pasted the refund email snippet below and attached screenshot to the expense app.

```
Airbnb: Partial refund issued
Host: acme-hosting
Original charge: $420.00 (txn id: AB-2026-9987)
Refund: $120.00 (refund id: RF-33421)
Date refund posted: 2026-03-06
```

zoe_ops: for clarity - when you submitted the expense for $300 did you set payment method = Corporate Card or Personal + Reimburse?

maria: Corporate Card. I figured net charge is what matters but the portal still shows $420.

ben_finance: bank reconciliation rules: we reimburse what's actually charged to the corporate card (post-refunds). If the card issuer hasn't posted the refund yet, we ask card provider to confirm pending credit. please do not claim personal reimbursement for a corp card charge.

maria: ok that makes sense. what's the timeline for the issuer to show the credit?

ben_finance: usually 3-5 business days for the merchant refund to post. if it hasn't posted in 7 days, we can open a query. @opsbot can you create SpendOps ticket for card-probing with label "card-refund" and link to expense id?

opsbot: Ticket created: SP-2026-505. Linked expense: EXP-2026-778. Please attach proof of refund email and card txn ids.

ben_finance: once the refund posts, we'll adjust the corporate card ledger and close the expense as approved for $300. if refund is denied, we'll need a host confirmation email stating no refund issued and then we escalate to manager approval for reimbursement.

maria: noted. one more: the refund came in EUR (host charged in EUR), but my card statement shows USD conversions. do we use the company daily FX rate or card provider rate?

ben_finance: policy: we use the card provider settled USD amount as the authoritative charge. capture both amounts in the expense line (original EUR and settled USD) so finance can reconcile. if you have the card settlement line showing the refund in USD that helps.

maria: uploaded the settlement screenshot showing refunded USD value RF-33421 -> $118.40 (rounded).

ben_finance: perfect. we'll wait for the issuer to post full refund. keeping SP-2026-505 open. i'll update this thread when it's resolved. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks everyone — will monitor and leave the expense pending until you confirm.
